feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (12 mm, y = 0.04) lost the oval line 2.15 times per run and sat at the 0.06 m floor on every track. Iteration 1 (0.03 m spacing) removed those losses but cut progress on every track (oval 0.19 to 0.115), so spread is not the lever. Iteration 2 (16 mm, y = 0.04) removed oval line losses (0.0), but progress stayed at 0.115 on the oval and 0.03 on the slalom, and max_error stayed at the floor. So the footprint fixed line loss, and the remaining limit looks like late steering. Integration work: sensor_weights stay at 25 times x, so the steering gain per metre is the same as the baseline, and kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0 and last_direction are unchanged. Keep the weights at 25 per metre if the spread changes again. If the next race shows oval progress above 0.19 with max_error below 0.06, the lead is working, so push it further. If steering_oscillation rises, the lead is too strong, so pull it back. If progress stays flat, the geometry lever is largely used up, and gains come next.
requested_changes: If the next race shows oval progress above 0.19 with max_error below 0.06 and steering_oscillation at or below 0.10, keep 16 mm sensors and the 0.16 m spread, and try the forward lead at y = 0.08 (the contract maximum). Evidence: iteration 2 showed the footprint removed line losses but progress stayed at 0.115, so the lead is the next lever to test.

If the next race shows steering_oscillation above the baseline 0.10 on the oval with completion intact, pull the lead back to y = 0.06 while keeping x = -0.08, -0.04, 0, 0.04, 0.08. Evidence: baseline oscillation was 0.10 on the oval and 0.08 on the s-bend, so a stronger lead may add jitter (Hypothesis B).

If the next race shows progress flat near 0.115 on the oval and max_error still at about 0.06 at y = 0.07, try wheel_track 0.10 to test whether turn authority limits corrections. Evidence: iterations 0 to 2 all kept progress near 0.115 with rms_error near 0.03, so turn response and not sensor position may be the limit.
